questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Other

questions.question: Please explain: *
questions.answer: I went on exchange to get an experience of a lifetime, meet new people and learn a new culture

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Warm weather, good travel opportunities, academic opportunities and recommendations from friends

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Studying abroad in San Diego has been the best five months of my life. I have had such amazing experiences and I've learned a lot about the American culture, American law, myself and life.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was quite easy. The Graduate & International Programs from USD contacted me often before my arrival and gave me the information I needed.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I didn't receive any assistance.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: The Graduate & International Programs had contacted me by email many times before I arrived in San Diego and they were very helpful.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was very difficult and it took several weeks before me and my fellow exchange students found a house together. We spent a lot of time searching online and calling various real estate agents. I lived in Mission Beach and I can highly recommend this. It was amazing!

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: When you live off campus, like Mission Beach, you get to live closer to the beach and you get to choose your own roommates. For me, this was the best decision ever. I would recommend students to live off campus in order to get the real "San Diego vibe".

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I did the course registration myself online, and it was very easy.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I had a e-mail exchange with a Academic Adviser, who helped me with the registration. If you don't like a course, you can change your courses after the beginning of the classes. I changed my registration several times, and it was very easy.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The Academic Adviser and the opportunity to change courses.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the classes I wanted

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Contact the Academic Adviser and make sure to get your registrations done in good time

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Some courses, like "Evidence" were really hard and not suitable for exchange students. I therefore changed from Evidence to the courses "International negotiations" and "Law at the movies". My best advice is to ask the American students for advice in regard to choosing courses. They are very helpful and can tell you which courses are hard, which professors are best and so on.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The style of teaching at USD is very different from the style at UCPH. The professors at USD use the Socratic Method, meaning that the professor asks students a question even though they have not raised their hand. This is very different from the danish teaching style, and is something that you have to get used to. Moreover, it's mandatory to come to class, in contrary to in Denmark.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Intro to U.S. Law, Interviewing & Counseling, Negotiation, International Negotiations, Law at the movies

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Negotiation was really interesting and professor Gregg Relyea was very competent. Interviewing & Counseling was also really good and is a nice course if you want to talk to a lot of other students and improve your english skills.

questions.answer: Travel (30.000 DKK)

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Housing, food and grocery shopping was more expensive than expected. California is a lot more expensive than Denmark, which I was very surprised about.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There were many different sport clubs and so on

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: The school arranged many events for international students, like bagel breakfast and theme dinners. There were many sport teams you could join including basketball, American football, baseball, soccer, softball and swimming.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend to join the ISO if you want to talk to other international students. I would also recommend to go to the annual "bar review", which is a party at one of the bars/clubs in san diego.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I would recommend to travel a lot. I were many different places including Los Angeles, Las Vegas, San Fransisco, Grand Canyon, Bryce Canyon, Antelope Canyon, Horseshoe Bend, Zion Nationalpark, Yosemite and Sequoia Nationalpark. I also traveled to Hawaii and Mexico. In San Diego, i would recommend to go to Sunset Cliffs, Torrey pines, Joshua Tree National park, see a basketball game, an American football game and a baseball game, go to Downtown especially to the Gaslamp District and Little Italy, see all the beautiful beaches at Mission Beach and see La Jolla. If they want to experience good night life they should go to Waterbar, Backyard, Moonshine and Thrusters!

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy since the Americans are very friendly and easy to talk to

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Reach out and talk to them - they are very interested in exchange students and ready to hang out

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: That the Americans are so friendly and open-minded. Its easy to get new friends in the US

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Say yes to every opportunity and engage yourself in all the social events. It's the best way to make new friends and you wont regret it.
2. Reach out to the Graduate & International Programs if you have any questions. They are very helpful.
3. Travel a lot, and see all the amazing things in California.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Don't be afraid to reach out to your professors if you want to discuss something in class, the exam and so on.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: My personal development and all the new friends I have gained

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Finding housing

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
